Development Approach

RAP (RESTful ABAP Programming) is used for all new development. Classic ABAP is not applied.

Dependencies and Prerequisites

  • ABAP Release 7.54 or higher.
  • OData V4 support.
  • Enable RAP Development in system profile.
  • Activate required SAP Fiori libraries.
  • Enable SAP ABAP Unit and SAP Test Suite for unit testing.

4. Database Table Definition

ABAP Dictionary Table

FieldTypeLengthDescription
OBJ_IDCHAR10Business Object ID
OBJ_NAMECHAR30Business Object Name
CREATED_BYCHAR12Creator
CREATED_ONDATE8Creation Date
CHANGED_BYCHAR12Last Modifier
CHANGED_ONDATE8Last Changed Date
STATUSCHAR20Object Status

Enhancement Category

None required for this table.

5. CDS View Layer for RAP

Interface View ZI_

@AbapCatalog.sqlViewName: 'ZIVIEW'
@AbapCatalog.compiler.compareFilter: true
@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #NOT_REQUIRED
@EndUserText.label: 'Z Interface View'
define view ZI_BusinessObject
  with parameters
    p_active as abap.bool
{
  key OBJ_ID      as Id,
       OBJ_NAME    as Name,
       CREATED_ON  as Created,
       CHANGED_ON  as Changed,
       STATUS      as Status
}
where p_active = true;

Projection View ZC_ with UI Annotations

@AbapCatalog.sqlViewName: 'ZCVIEW'
@AbapCatalog.compiler.compareFilter: true
@EndUserText.label: 'Z Projection View'
@UI.dataCategory: #DYNAMIC
@UI.lineItem: [
  { position: 1, label: 'Object ID',   importance: #HIGH   },
  { position: 2, label: 'Object Name', importance: #HIGH   },
  { position: 3, label: 'Created On',  importance: #MEDIUM },
  { position: 4, label: 'Status',      importance: #MEDIUM }
]
define view ZC_BusinessObject
  as select from ZI_BusinessObject
{
  key Id      as OBJ_ID,
       Name    as OBJ_NAME,
       Created as CREATED_ON,
       Status  as OBJ_STATUS
}

Metadata Extension for Fiori

No additional metadata extensions are required for this implementation.

Mars AI Use Cases Catalogue – DRAFT

Executive Summary AI Maturity Assessment SAP AI Landscape Overview Use Cases Catalogue Quick Wins Implementation Roadmap Investment & ROI Summary Responsible AI Next Steps

Executive Summary

Marshmallow, Mars, Incorporated – a global leader in confectionery, petcare, and nutrition – faces a rapidly evolving market with rising consumer demands for personalization, sustainability, and operational excellence. Leveraging SAP’s comprehensive AI ecosystem (Joule, AI Core, Build Apps, Generative AI Hub) offers transformative opportunities across Finance, Materials Management, Sales & Distribution, Human Resources, and the SAP Business Technology Platform. This catalogue identifies 20 prioritized AI use cases, each mapped to business processes, technology layers, ROI estimates, complexity ratings, and prerequisites, enabling Mars to accelerate digital transformation while maintaining responsible AI governance.

AI Maturity Assessment

Dimension Current State Target State (FY28)
Data Readiness Moderately clean, siloed across legacy systems Enterprise‑wide master data governance with unified data lake
Model Development Ad-hoc ML models in Python notebooks Continuous delivery of validated models via SAP AI Core
Deployment & Operations Manual model monitoring Automated model lifecycle management with observability
AI Adoption Culture Limited AI literacy AI champions across all functional areas, embedded in workflows

SAP AI Landscape Overview

  • SAP Joule: Data‑centric compute platform enabling real‑time AI analytics and automated data pipelines.
  • SAP AI Core: End‑to‑end AI platform for model training, governance, and deployment across SAP S/4HANA and BTP.
  • SAP Build Apps AI: Low‑code application development with AI‑powered UI, NLP, and workflow automation.
  • Generative AI Hub: Plug‑and‑play generative models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) integrated via APIs for rapid prototyping.

These pillars interlock to provide Mars with a unified, secure, and scalable AI ecosystem, ready for both predictive analytics and generative experiences.

Prioritized Use Cases Catalogue

UC15 Fraud Detection in Supplier Payments Finance AI Core (ML) $3.5M annual fraud avoidance Medium 84 Payment data, anomaly detection model, SAP FICO integration
UC16 Workforce Skill Gap Analysis Human Resources Joule ML + BTP Analytics $1.2M annual productivity gains Medium 82 Learning & Development data, skill taxonomy, model governance
UC17 Product Lifecycle Cost Modeling Engineering & R&D Joule ML + BTP Analytics $2M savings on new product launch Low 78 R&D cost data, product specs, model validation
UC18 Chatbot for Customer Order Tracking Customer Service Build Apps AI + GenAI $1.5M annual CSO reduction, 15% NPS uplift High 91 Order data, API integration, compliance policies
UC19 Compliance Alerting for Regulatory Changes Governance GenAI + BTP Workflow $2M annual risk avoidance Medium 83 Regulatory feed, compliance rules, workflow engine
UC20 Plant Yield Forecasting for Agricultural Inputs Supply Chain Joule ML + IoT $3M annual cost reduction, 12% yield improvement Medium 86 Agricultural sensor data, weather APIs, model governance

Quick Wins – Top 5 Use Cases for 90‑Day Implementation

  1. UC02 – Automated Invoice Matching (Finance)
  2. UC06 – HR Chatbot (HR)
  3. UC13 – Warehouse Layout Optimization (MM)
  4. UC18 – Customer Order Tracking Chatbot (CS)
  5. UC11 – Dynamic Pricing Engine (SD)

These initiatives require minimal data re‑engineering, have low to medium complexity, and deliver immediate ROI.

Implementation Roadmap

The roadmap follows a phased approach to balance risk, speed, and business impact.

  1. Phase 0 – Foundation (Months 0‑3)
    • Data lake establishment via SAP Joule
    • Model governance framework in AI Core
    • AI literacy workshops across Mars units
  2. Phase 1 – Quick Wins (Months 3‑6)
    • Deploy UC02, UC06, UC13, UC18, UC11
    • Implement monitoring dashboards in BTP
    • Establish continuous delivery pipelines
  3. Phase 2 – Enterprise Scale (Months 6‑12)
    • Roll out UC01, UC03, UC04, UC05, UC07, UC08, UC09, UC10, UC14, UC15, UC16, UC17, UC19, UC20
    • Integrate AI solutions with SAP S/4HANA and Ariba
    • Governance & compliance audits
  4. Phase 3 – Continuous Innovation (Months 12‑24)
    • Introduce generative AI services for new product ideation
    • Expand AI to emerging markets and new business lines
    • Implement AI ethics council and responsible AI framework

Investment & ROI Summary

Below is a high‑level estimate of capital and operating expenditures versus projected returns over five years.

Year Capital Expenditure (USD) Operating Expenditure (USD) Annual Incremental Revenue (USD) Net Savings (USD)

FY29 15M 12M 140M 118M
FY30 10M 8M 160M 142M
FY31 5M 6M 180M 169M
FY32 3M 4M 200M 193M

ROI: >20× over five years, with a payback period of approximately 1.2 years.

Responsible AI – Draft Considerations

  • Transparency: Model documentation, explainability dashboards for key decision points.
  • Fairness: Bias audits for supplier risk and credit scoring models.
  • Privacy: GDPR and CCPA compliance for customer data in GenAI applications.
  • Accountability: AI steering committee with cross‑functional representation.
  • Security: Zero‑trust API gateways for GenAI integration.
  • Governance: AI Core model registry with versioning and rollback.

All AI initiatives will be reviewed by the Responsible AI Office before production rollout.

Next Steps

  1. Obtain executive sign‑off on the investment thesis.
  2. Kick‑off Phase 0 data lake and governance workshops.
  3. Prioritize use cases with the highest strategic impact and quick‑win potential.
  4. Set up a cross‑functional AI implementation task force.
  5. Schedule a pilot for UC02 and UC06 within the next 30 days.
